result.strongest_objection: The MUT-GET-SERVED mutation violates the rule-3i discipline because it is vacuous. M108-4 states this mutation expects the test to RED because 'GET must answer 405, not 200'. However, as verified in V9 and acknowledged in D108-6 ('the seam's internal writeMethodNotAllowed is the same observable'), the upstream `mcphttp` seam natively hard-refuses non-POST requests. Mutating the World `ServeMux` to pass GET requests to the handler will therefore still result in a 405 generated by `mcphttp`. The test will continue to pass, meaning the mutation survives. A World-level route mutation cannot force this upstream seam to serve a 200 on GET.
result.catch: MUT-GET-SERVED cannot turn the test RED because mcphttp natively returns 405 for GET regardless of the ServeMux registration pattern.
result.proposed_fix: Replace MUT-GET-SERVED with MUT-MUX-METHOD-REMOVED (mutating the registration from 'POST /mcp/' to '/mcp/') and either have `TestMCPGetRefused` strictly assert a byte-level difference between Go's ServeMux 405 body and the seam's 405 body, or replace the network test entirely with a source-level AST scan asserting that the exact literal 'POST /mcp/' is passed to `mux.HandleFunc`.

result.strongest_objection: The doc's entire callback/timing model — V33 ('one tools/call POST runs up to THREE sequential hostcall.Run calls'), D108-5's 'one slot at a time', D108-9's 'the second NewRequest in a POST', and the D108-10 budget table whose 3+10+20=33 s arithmetic is the whole answer to the quorum's r1 REJECT — models exactly one JSON-RPC request per POST. Yet the doc itself states the seam implements '2025-03-26 batch handling' (and the default negotiated version is 2025-03-26, the version WITH batching). For a batch POST carrying N tools/call items the dispatch side is N Invoke callbacks, not one, and NOTHING in the doc verifies or bounds that shape: V33's cited reads (handler.go:60-135, methods.go:60-105) never reference the batch dispatch site, so 'the seam runs its callbacks sequentially' is asserted, not verified; per-item error semantics (does one failed Invoke fail the WHOLE batch with the frozen envelope, or does the seam return per-item results?) are unexamined; slot occupancy under a batch (sequential → one slot at a time, concurrent → up to 8) is unconstrained against the D108-5 rationale; and neither the conformance suite (AC-WIRE-108's leg list: SSE frame, 202, 400s, 4 MiB, envelope, initialize/ping) nor the production-constants leg nor any mutation covers an N-item batch. The aggregate ctx does still bound a batch POST at 20 s, so the safety property survives by a mechanism the doc never derives in writing — which is precisely the r1 failure mode (an un-derived composition claim) one level down, at the exact composition point the quorum already rejected once.
result.catch: Verify the batch path first-party and amend the central model: read the batch dispatch branch in mcphttp (methods.go / wherever the 2025-03-26 batch is handled) and record (a) whether batch items dispatch sequentially or concurrently through hostcall.Run, (b) whether the authorize-time ResolveSession+Tools pair runs ONCE per POST or per batch item, (c) whether a failed item callback yields the whole-POST frozen envelope or a per-item JSON-RPC error entry, (d) per-item snapshot/task-id/journal-row accounting against D108-8/D108-9. Then correct V33's 'up to THREE sequential hostcall.Run calls per POST' (false for the default version's batch shape), add a batch row to the D108-10 budget table (2 + N Runs; each invoke bounded by min(invokeDeadline, aggregate remainder); fail-fast after aggregate expiry), extend AC-WIRE-108/AC-BOUNDS-108 with a batch conformance leg (e.g., a 3-item batch of ping+tools/call+unknown-name observed from the mount, plus a multi-invoke batch in the production-constants leg), and add a batch mutation (e.g., MUT-BATCH-PARTIAL pinning whole-envelope-vs-per-item semantics, and extend MUT-AGGREGATE-REMOVED's killer to a batch shape). If the batch path dispatches concurrently, re-derive D108-5's 'one slot at a time' and the slot-cap-8 alignment accordingly; if the seam offers no way to refuse batches, that admission must be recorded as a scoped residual rather than left unmodeled.
result.proposed_fix: Add V37 [R]: 'the batch dispatch path: N request items per POST dispatch K Invoke callbacks (K = count of tools/call items), <sequentially|concurrently>, with per-item error semantics <whole-POST WriteMCPEnvelope | per-item error entry>, and authorize (ResolveSession+Tools+CallerSurface) runs exactly once per POST' — command: sed/grep over the batch branch in .../ailang@v0.47.2/serveapi/protocol/mcphttp/methods.go and handler.go with line cites and a same-call control (the single-request callTool site at methods.go:83-85 already read). Rewrite V33's claim to '2 hostcall.Run calls per POST at authorize + 1 per tools/call item (batch: K invokes)'. Insert into the D108-10 budget table: '| batch POST (K invokes) | ≤ 20 s | each invoke min(invokeDeadline inner, Runner, aggregate remainder); after aggregate expiry each pending Run short-circuits on parent ctx (runner.go:47-49) | inside the aggregate |'. Add to M108-4/AC-WIRE-108: TestMCPBatchConformance (3-item batch: ping + valid tools/call + unknown-name → assert the seam's real batch response shape from the mount) plus a batch leg in TestMCPPostBudgetProductionConstants with K>1 invokes, and mutations MUT-BATCH-PARTIAL (flip per-item error semantics → batch conformance REDs) and an extended MUT-AGGREGATE-REMOVED batch leg. Amend D108-8/9: one admission snapshot + one task id + one journal row PER BATCH ITEM (state whether K snapshots hit the StoreReader cache and whether journal cost per POST is now O(K)). If V37 finds concurrent dispatch, replace D108-5's 'one slot at a time' with the per-POST slot occupancy bound (min(K, 8)) and restate the procbound-alignment rationale accordingly.
